chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali from his father from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from one who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The sick person prays sitting; if he is unable, he prays lying on his back, saying Takbir then reciting. When he intends to bow (ruku'), he closes his eyes, then glorifies (subhan), then opens his eyes, and the opening of his eyes is the raising of his head from ruku'. When he intends to prostrate (sujud), he closes his eyes, then glorifies; when he has glorified, he opens his eyes, and the opening of his eyes is the raising of his head from sujud. Then he recites the Tashahhud and concludes (salams).
ai.seo_question: How should a sick person perform the bowing and prostration parts of prayer if they cannot move their head?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific ritual procedure for a sick person unable to stand or bow fully, prescribing that prayer be performed while lying down. It innovatively utilizes the closing and opening of the eyes to signify the transitions of ruku' and sujud, thereby preserving the essential elements of prayer (arkan) through gesture (ikhtiyar) when physical movement is impossible. This method reflects the Shia juristic principle of adapting worship to the patient's capacity without invalidating the prayer's structure.
